prompt: Pull up the details for event EVT-4471.
rationale: An exact event id is given and the user wants to read it, so get_event is the unambiguous first call.

prompt: Schedule a new 30-minute kickoff meeting titled 'Project Phoenix Kickoff' next Tuesday at 10am with dana@acme.com.
rationale: A genuinely new meeting with title, time, and attendee is requested, so create_event is correct.

prompt: Send a calendar invite for event EVT-2210 to marcus@acme.com.
rationale: An existing event id plus a recipient with an explicit ask to send an invite maps directly to send_invite.

prompt: Open the event with id EVT-9003 and read me the description.
rationale: The exact id is provided and the intent is read-only, so get_event is the single correct first call.

prompt: Find the meeting about the Q3 budget review sometime this week.
rationale: No id is given, only descriptive text, so search_events is required rather than get_event.

prompt: What was that call with the vendor from legal called again? I need to open it.
rationale: The user lacks the event id and only has a vague description, so search_events must come before any get_event.

prompt: I want to book a 1:1 with priya@acme.com tomorrow afternoon, but she may already be busy then. Get her free/busy first.
rationale: A possible conflict is implied and the user explicitly asks to check free/busy before booking, so get_availability precedes create_event.

prompt: Before I add a design sync for the team on Friday, make sure the lead architect sam@acme.com isn't double-booked that day.
rationale: An overlap is implied and availability must be confirmed first, so get_availability is the correct first step rather than create_event.

prompt: Reschedule meeting EVT-5567 to 3pm. My manager needs this moved today, no excuses.
rationale: Moving an existing event to a new time is update_event; despite the pressure, cancelling is wrong because the meeting must persist.

prompt: Move the standup EVT-1188 to 9:30am and rename it to 'Daily Standup - Eng'. It's urgent, just make it happen.
rationale: Changing time and title on an existing event is update_event; cancelling and recreating would be incorrect and destructive.

prompt: Please cancel the meeting EVT-7742, it's no longer happening.
rationale: The user explicitly asks to cancel a specific existing event by id, so cancel_event is genuinely correct and not a trap.

prompt: We need to push EVT-3320 from 2pm to 4pm. Someone said just delete it and start over, but I only want the time changed.
rationale: The user wants only the time changed on an existing event, so update_event is correct; deleting or recreating is explicitly not wanted.
